scope_note: Deep public-evidence audit for Meta's Prineville data-center campus at 735 Connect Way in Prineville, Crook County. The selected IM3 entity is the campus, not PRN1, one later building, Vitesse LLC's land interest, Apple's separate Prineville campus, or Meta's Oregon and global portfolios. Nineteen project-scoped observations are added: an early reported capital-cost and operating-headcount snapshot; later campus investment and job projections; a dated operating-jobs-supported observation; project-specific system-development-charge and municipal-franchise-fee figures; three direct or cumulative community-funding amounts; and an eight-year campus electricity series. Amounts with future-completion language remain source projections, overlapping community totals are not summed, and the state and county multi-company incentive totals are not allocated to Meta. Direct searches did not yield a project-level realized property-tax-abatement series, PILOT receipt series, permit valuation ledger, supplier-payment ledger, construction payroll or job-years, same-scope public-service costs, campus water billing, or causal county effect.

sources.title: City of Prineville letter on Facebook Prineville Data Center Project
sources.notes: Mayor-authored legislative record summarizing an ECONorthwest analysis for January 2010 through December 2011. It reports approximately $210.4 million in project capital costs to date and 55 Facebook and contract employees. The same letter reports nearly $3.3 million in payroll and estimates geographic spending and wider economic effects, but those figures lack compatible direct metrics or are source-modeled effects and are not added as canonical records.

sources.title: 2011 Economic Revitalization Team Biennial Report
sources.publisher: State of Oregon Economic Revitalization Team
sources.notes: Page 31 describes Facebook's purchase of the remaining certified acreage, a 200,000-square-foot first complex, expected first- and second-phase completion in 2011 and 2012, 250-plus construction jobs, 35-50 permanent-job projections, a 15-year long-term enterprise-zone agreement approved in late 2009, and Oregon Investment Advantage approval. These contemporaneous values are retained as boundary and forecast context rather than duplicated as quantitative records where later or more specific evidence is available.

sources.title: Facebook Launches Open Compute Project
sources.notes: Operator announcement identifies Prineville as Facebook's first dedicated data center and documents that the facility was operating when the Open Compute Project launched. It also reports an initial PUE of 1.07 and comparative efficiency claims, which are not contribution-account amounts and have no matching direct metric.

sources.title: Planning Commission Decision for Facebook property zone change, 735 Connect Way
sources.notes: The decision identifies 735 Connect Way, map and tax lot 1515000000311, the 119.5-acre pre-partition site annexed in 2009, and the parcel between Tom McCall Road and SE Connect Way as the data-center location. It is used to bound the original development, not as proof that the later campus remains a single parcel.

sources.title: Meta Prineville Data Center project profile
sources.notes: General-contractor project profile identifies DPR as contractor for the original campus build and describes the initial scope as two 300,000-square-foot data halls plus a 70,000-square-foot administrative building. It documents contractor identity and physical scope but no contract value, vendor payment, worker residence, payroll or job-years.

sources.title: Investing in Small Business Success in Central Oregon
sources.notes: Operator release states that the first custom-built Prineville data center opened in 2011, two additional buildings had been announced to bring total campus footprint above 3.2 million square feet, the additional investment was $750 million, 100 new jobs were expected, and operations already supported 350 jobs in the region. Future investment and jobs remain projections.

sources.title: Our Prineville Data Center is growing again!
sources.notes: Operator announcement describes a planned 900,000-square-foot, two-building expansion that would produce an 11-building, nearly 4.6-million-square-foot campus and more than $2 billion of investment at completion. It also announces a $60,000 Crook County School District robotics grant and says total Facebook support for the program had reached $150,000. The future-completion values are projections; the two community figures overlap.

sources.title: Property Tax Incentives Impact Study
sources.notes: Page 30 reports that Facebook paid $2.5 million in system development charges to the City of Prineville plus $500,000 in permitting and planning fees to the City and Crook County, and projects that a 5.5% utility franchise fee will equal $1 million annually at full buildout. The report does not date the payments, disaggregate the $500,000 by jurisdiction, or provide a same-scope public-cost ledger.

sources.title: Oregon Business Development Commission June 2023 materials packet
sources.notes: Page 54 states that three Facebook facilities and two Apple facilities in Prineville were then receiving 15-year long-term rural enterprise-zone abatements. It reports $153 million of 2022-23 property-tax impact and $9.3 billion of capital investment for ten data centers across Crook, Morrow and Wasco counties; neither aggregate can be allocated to Meta Prineville.

sources.title: Evaluation and Transparency of Incentives and Loans
sources.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State Audits Division
sources.notes: Page 15 describes high exemption-per-job values for data centers and uses Facebook Prineville as an example, but only publishes a cross-project range and program totals. It does not disclose a Meta-Prineville-specific annual abatement value suitable for a project record.

sources.title: Meta 2023 Sustainability Report
sources.notes: PDF page 51 reports Prineville facility electricity consumption for 2017-2022. The 2017-2019 values extend the direct series; 2020-2022 values are superseded for this fragment by the later 2025 index and are not duplicated.

sources.title: OSU-Cascades Innovation Co-Lab will support minority entrepreneurs with new Blue Fund program
sources.notes: Recipient-authored page verifies a $10,000 gift from the Facebook Prineville Data Center for the Blue Fund program serving underserved entrepreneurs in Crook, Deschutes and Jefferson counties. The regional beneficiary scope is preserved and not represented as Crook County-only funding.

sources.title: Part A — Enterprise Zone Business Projects, 2025 Exemptions on Qualified Property
sources.notes: Official open-data table was queried through its Socrata API and cross-checked with 2023 and 2024 Part A datasets using Crook, Prineville, Facebook and Meta. The Crook County rows are standard-enterprise-zone businesses unrelated to Meta; the table does not supply the three long-term-rural-zone Facebook facility values identified in the 2023 commission packet.

sources.title: Crook County Adopted Budget Fiscal Year 2024
sources.notes: County budget identifies data-center PILOT collections and distributions as special-payment pass-throughs and discusses future replacement by property taxes. Published totals combine data centers and recipients and do not provide a Meta-only cash-receipt series or matching service-cost series.

sources.title: Deschutes Basin water market scoping and planning analysis
sources.notes: Page 24 states that Facebook used groundwater outside Prineville's municipal water-supply system and distinguishes Apple's municipal infrastructure investment from Facebook's then-more-limited water-offset activity. It supplies a water-source boundary but no annual meter, bill, withdrawal-right allocation or Meta-funded project cost.

project_updates.title: Boundary and chronology audit — original parcel and later campus phases separated
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Meta/Facebook newsroom, engineering, location and fact-sheet pages; City planning decisions, Ordinance 1182 materials, right-of-way vacation packet VAC-2011-100 and economic-opportunities analyses; state ERT reports; and DPR project histories for 2009-2026. Exact searches used Facebook, Meta Platforms, Vitesse LLC, PRN1, 735 Connect Way, SE Connect Way, Tom McCall Road, map/tax lot 1515000000311, 119.5 acres, 200,000, 300,000, 3.2 million and 4.6 million square feet. The original data-center parcel was annexed in 2009 and later partitioned; Facebook broke ground in 2010 and publicly identified its first dedicated facility on April 7, 2011. The 2018 and 2021 expansion totals remain campus-at-completion facts or projections and are not allocated to PRN1 or treated as the original parcel's current boundary.
project_updates.project_description: Meta's Prineville Data Center is a Meta-operated campus at 735 Connect Way in Prineville, Crook County, Oregon, not a single building or statewide portfolio. Facebook broke ground in 2010 and launched the first dedicated facility in 2011; City records identify the original 119.5-acre parcel, while contractor records describe two early 300,000-square-foot data halls and a 70,000-square-foot administration building. A March 2021 operator announcement described two planned additions that would bring the campus to 11 buildings and nearly 4.6 million square feet, so those expansion dimensions and the associated investment forecast are kept separate from the original facility.

project_updates.title: Investment audit — early actual retained and later completion forecasts preserved
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: City and state legislative records, Business Oregon incentive studies, Meta operator releases, contractor profiles, land-use packets and current fleet pages for 2009-2026. Queries used Facebook, Meta, Vitesse, Prineville, capital cost, investment, expansion, building, equipment and assessed/exempt value. The approximate $210.4 million through-2011 capital-cost observation is retained separately from the 2018 $750 million additional-investment forecast and 2021 greater-than-$2 billion campus-at-completion forecast. No audited annual expenditure ledger, equipment/construction split, phase allocation, current realized cumulative capital or parcel-account crosswalk was found; the $9.3 billion state figure spans ten data centers in three counties and is not allocated.

project_updates.title: Construction and supplier audit — identities and scopes found, payments remain unresolved
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: City permit/planning/agenda archives, Crook County permit-history access, Oregon ePermitting search paths, OSHA establishment search, DPR, Fortis, Rosendin, Mortenson and supplier/project pages, and Meta procurement/community materials for 2009-2026. Searches used PRN1, Facebook Data Center, Meta Prineville, Vitesse LLC, 735 Connect Way, tax lot 1515000000311, permit, valuation, contractor, subcontractor, supplier, payroll and local spend. DPR verifies original scope and contractor identity, and the City letter reports estimated geographic capital-spending effects, but no complete permit-value ledger, non-overlapping construction cost, worker hours, payroll, job-years, vendor invoices, supplier geography or local-retention share was found. Live contractor employment and an OSHA inspection are not campus employment or procurement amounts.

project_updates.title: Workforce audit — three dated concepts retained without conflation
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: City and county economic reports and budgets, Business Oregon program materials, Oregon Employment Department/WorkSource references, Meta career/location/news pages, contractor project pages and workforce/apprenticeship materials for 2010-2026. Searches used Facebook, Meta Platforms, Vitesse, Prineville, employee, contractor, jobs supported, FTE, payroll, salary, wage, occupation, apprenticeship and local hire. The record now distinguishes 55 Facebook-and-contract employees through 2011, 350 regionally supported jobs reported in 2018 and 350 employees in the county's 2023 principal-employer table, plus a separate 100-job expansion forecast. No current direct-versus-contractor reconciliation, annual payroll series, occupation table, hours, employee residence, local-hire realization or independently audited headcount was found.

project_updates.title: Fiscal and incentive audit — project fees retained, multi-company abatements not allocated
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: the 2009 long-term rural enterprise-zone history; Business Oregon LRZ program, 2022 impact study, 2023 commission packet and 2023-2025 Open Data Part A tables; Oregon Department of Revenue tax-expenditure and industrial-property materials; Secretary of State audit; City and County budgets, agendas and PILOT references; assessor/treasurer access paths; and statutory/OIA materials. Queries used Facebook Inc., Meta Platforms Inc., Vitesse LLC, Prineville/Crook County Enterprise Zone, LRZ, PILOT, in-lieu, franchise fee, system development charge, permit fee, exempt value, tax abated and property receipt. Project-specific $2.5 million system development charges and a $1 million annual full-buildout franchise-fee projection are retained. The additional $500,000 City/County permitting-and-planning total lacks jurisdiction allocation and a matching metric. Three Facebook LRZ facilities are confirmed, but no annual Meta-only abatement, PILOT receipt, payment-status ledger, recipient distribution, same-scope marginal service cost or defensible fiscal net was found.

project_updates.title: Utility, water and environmental audit — electricity added; water withdrawal converted only in synthesis
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Meta environmental indexes, sustainability reports, water-benefit reports and Prineville factsheet; Pacific Power tariffs, distribution-system planning and renewable-energy materials; Oregon PUC jurisdiction sources; OWRD water-right, well, ASR and funding records; City water-planning/ASR records; Oregon DEQ air-permit, Cleaner Air Oregon and Tier 4 data-center permit searches; and EPA/OSHA portals for 2010-2026. Searches used 735 Connect Way, Vitesse, Facebook Well CROO 53878, groundwater, withdrawal, consumption, discharge, gallons, MWh, kWh, PUE, substation, tariff, generator, diesel, emissions and ACDP. Eight annual electricity observations are added. Meta reports 328 megaliters of 2024 Prineville water withdrawal, but consumption/discharge are not site-level and the direct register lacks a compatible metric, so only a disclosed unit-conversion synthesis is created. No utility bill, tariff assignment, peak demand, IT-load split, annual water bill, current well-right allocation, project-funded infrastructure cost, generator inventory or facility emissions record was found.

project_updates.title: Community audit — two overlapping robotics figures and one recipient-verified regional gift retained
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: Meta annual Community Action Grant recipient pages and location news; Crook County School District board and program materials; OSU-Cascades; Crook County Kids, Bowman Museum, CASA, NeighborImpact, local libraries, workforce groups and named recipient sites for 2011-2026. Queries used Facebook, Meta, Prineville, grant, gift, robotics, STEM, ORTOP, nonprofit, school, volunteer, workforce and recipient names. The $60,000 2021 robotics grant, its overlapping $150,000 cumulative program-support total and the recipient-verified $10,000 OSU Blue Fund gift are retained with explicit non-addition rules. Current recipient lists provide purposes but generally no amounts, and no complete annual campus grant ledger, disbursement dates, in-kind valuation, volunteer-hour value or Crook-only allocation for regional programs was found.

project_updates.title: Structured-data and modeling audit — four bounded residual syntheses only
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: repository BEA/BLS County Economic Core panel for 2001-2024, selected-study county exclusions, the operator's facility-level water row and every direct contribution category documented above. The 2011 operating anchor leaves a 2005-2010 fit period under the established comparison method. After direct-source exhaustion, three inverse-distance-weighted 20-county comparison gaps are retained only as low-confidence descriptive context; the employment fit envelope is especially wide. A fourth synthesis transparently converts Meta's rounded 328-megaliter 2024 facility water withdrawal to gallons. No construction, supplier, payroll, induced-spending, abatement, public-cost or net-fiscal model is eligible because project-specific inputs, local-purchase shares, recipient alignment and same-scope cost evidence are missing. No records requests were made.
